title: Estate file policy: what must be proved before a realised file is removed

criteria.text: THE DEHYDRATION GATE. No dehydration path removes any file while any declared precondition is unmet. This criterion is the estate's single carrier -- exactly one may exist project-wide, and a second anywhere makes every dehydration refuse. It asserts nothing itself; it names what must be true. <<PRECONDITIONS AC-00.2 AC-00.3 AC-00.4 PRECONDITIONS>>

state.evidence: The gate is declared and demonstrably bites. Measured 7 Sep in the scratch clone: with one precondition unsatisfied it refused, naming it -- '2 checked of 2 declared, 1 unmet: AC-00.7 (not satisfied)' -- and removed nothing; with the preconditions met the same command removed 9 files. A gate observed refusing AND passing, rather than one only ever seen to refuse.

criteria.text: CANON IS THE SOURCE AND A REALISED FILE IS A VIEW. Before a thread's files are removed, intent/.canon/st/<ID>.json must hold that thread whole -- objective, context, work packages, criteria, tests and attachments -- so dehydration discards a rendering and never the only copy. This is the precondition that makes the other two worth having: if canon were partial, a byte-perfect round trip would only prove the renderer is deterministic about the half it still has.

state.evidence: Read 7 Sep from intent/.canon/st/ST0011.json, the thread about to be dehydrated: objective 1275 chars, context 15069 chars, 6 work packages, 11 criteria, 10 tests, 1 attachment -- the whole thread, against 9 rendered files on disk holding no field canon lacks.

criteria.text: THE ROUND TRIP IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. dehydrate followed by hydrate returns every removed file byte for byte, compared by checksum against a baseline taken before the removal. Asserted from a real run on a real thread, never from the verb's success message -- this estate has already been bitten by intent sync --to-store reporting 'store replaced from the canon extract' while reverting the edit, so a verb's own report of success is not evidence about the disk.

state.evidence: Measured 7 Sep on a git clone of this repo at 6608d3d, in the scratchpad, so nothing in the working tree was at risk. Baseline sha256 of all 9 ST0011 files taken; intent st dehydrate ST0011 removed all 9; intent st hydrate ST0011 restored 9; the two checksum manifests diff clean and git status over intent/st/ST0011 is empty. Both nets checked, not one.

criteria.text: DEHYDRATION RUNS ON A COMMITTED TREE, so version control is a second and independent net beneath hydrate. The two nets fail differently on purpose: hydrate restores from canon and would carry a canon defect with it, while git restores bytes and knows nothing about canon. A run on a dirty tree has neither -- it mixes removals it can undo with edits it cannot.

state.evidence: Practice, and checkable per run: the tree is committed to a clean git status before organise --apply is invoked, so every removed file is recoverable from HEAD independently of hydrate. Verified immediately before the 7 Sep run that removed ST0011's files.
